name: Roe v. Wade
kicker: 1973 Supreme Court abortion ruling · Overruled by Dobbs in 2022
briefing: _Roe v. Wade_ is one of the most famous and most debated Supreme Court cases in U.S. history. In 1973, the Court ruled 7–2 for “Jane Roe,” a Texas woman whose real name was Norma McCorvey, holding that a constitutional right to privacy covers a woman’s decision whether to have an abortion. In 2022, the Court overruled Roe in _Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization_, returning the question of abortion laws to the states.
answerHtml: Roe v. Wade (prompt on “Roe” or “Wade” alone; do not accept “abortion”)
reject: dobbs v jackson womens health organization

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Sarah Weddington, who was only 26 when she first argued this case before the Supreme Court, and Linda Coffee represented its plaintiff, a Texas woman named Norma McCorvey. To protect her privacy, the plaintiff was given a pseudonym in this case.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 Supreme Court decision that was overruled by _Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization_.

tossups.p: The defendant in this case was a Texas district attorney whose office had prosecuted Jack Ruby, the man who shot Lee Harvey Oswald. That district attorney served Dallas County for more than thirty years.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 Supreme Court case about abortion and the right to privacy.

tossups.p: This case was argued twice before the Supreme Court, in December 1971 and October 1972, because Lewis Powell and William Rehnquist [“REN-kwist”] joined the Court after the first argument. In the 7–2 decision, Rehnquist and Byron White dissented.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 case about the right to privacy and abortion.

tossups.p: On the same day it decided this case, the Supreme Court also struck down parts of a Georgia law in a companion case, _Doe v. Bolton_, which was brought by a woman using the name “Mary Doe.” Justice Harry Blackmun wrote the majority opinions in both cases.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 decision that struck down a Texas law restricting abortion.

tossups.p: The author of this decision’s majority opinion had worked as a lawyer for the Mayo Clinic before Richard Nixon appointed him to the Supreme Court. That justice, Harry Blackmun, based this decision on a right to privacy.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 case that the Supreme Court overruled in 2022.

tossups.p: A 1992 joint opinion by Sandra Day O’Connor, Anthony Kennedy, and David Souter kept the core of this decision but replaced its trimester framework with an “undue burden” test. That case, _Planned Parenthood v. Casey_, involved a Pennsylvania law.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 decision about abortion, written by Harry Blackmun.

tossups.p: In May 2022, the news site _Politico_ published a leaked draft of a Supreme Court opinion that would overrule this decision. The final opinion, written by Samuel Alito, upheld a Mississippi law and returned the question of abortion laws to the states.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 case that was overruled in _Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization_.

tossups.p: This decision built on _Griswold v. Connecticut_, a 1965 case in which Justice William O. Douglas wrote that guarantees in the Bill of Rights have “penumbras” that create zones of privacy. Douglas also joined the majority in this decision.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 Supreme Court case that struck down a Texas abortion law.

tossups.p: The plaintiff in this case later revealed her identity, and in 1995 she announced that she had changed her views and would work with groups that opposed this decision. That plaintiff, Norma McCorvey, had used a pseudonym when the case began in Texas.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 Supreme Court case decided by a 7–2 vote.

tossups.p: This decision created a framework that divided pregnancy into three trimesters and allowed states to regulate abortion more as a pregnancy went on. Nineteen years later, the Supreme Court dropped that framework but kept the core of this decision.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 case named for a Texas plaintiff and a Dallas district attorney.

tossups.p: Chief Justice Warren Burger and Thurgood Marshall were among the seven justices in the majority in this decision, which was announced on January 22, 1973. Its majority opinion traced the history of laws on its subject all the way back to ancient Greece and Rome.
tossups.r: It said a right to privacy covers a woman’s decision whether to have an abortion. For 10 points, name this case that the Supreme Court overruled in 2022.

tossups.p: The case that overruled this decision was named for Thomas Dobbs, Mississippi’s top state health officer, and a clinic in the state’s capital. That 2022 ruling said that the Constitution does not grant a right to abortion and left the question to the states.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 decision, written by Harry Blackmun, that the _Dobbs_ case overruled.

tossups.p: In 1970, a three-judge federal court in Dallas declared the law challenged in this case unconstitutional but did not order Texas to stop enforcing it. The Supreme Court then struck down that law, which banned abortion except to save the woman’s life.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 Supreme Court decision, written by Harry Blackmun, about the right to privacy.

tossups.p: The lower court in this case found a right to privacy in the Ninth Amendment, but the Supreme Court’s majority said that right was founded in the Fourteenth Amendment’s concept of personal liberty. Harry Blackmun wrote that majority opinion.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 case about abortion that the Court overruled in 2022.

tossups.p: When the Supreme Court overruled this decision in 2022, Stephen Breyer, Sonia Sotomayor, and Elena Kagan wrote a joint dissent, while Chief Justice John Roberts voted to uphold the state law without overruling this decision.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1973 decision that had recognized a constitutional right to abortion.

trap.title: Which abortion case?
trap.body: Three Supreme Court cases come up together. _Roe v. Wade_ (1973) recognized a constitutional right to abortion; _Planned Parenthood v. Casey_ (1992) kept that right but replaced Roe’s trimester framework with an “undue burden” test; and _Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization_ (2022) overruled both and returned the issue to the states. Answering only “abortion,” or naming the wrong case, will not get credit.
trap.fix: Listen for the year and the names: 1973, Harry Blackmun, “Jane Roe,” Henry Wade, Texas, and trimesters mean _Roe v. Wade_; 1992, Pennsylvania, and “undue burden” mean _Casey_; 2022, Mississippi, Samuel Alito, and the leaked draft mean _Dobbs_.
trap.line: Real answer line: Roe v. Wade (do not accept “abortion” alone)
